summary: The link URL is built from the label instead of the target. `[[Getting Started|read the guide]]` links to /read_the_guide/, not /Getting_Started/. This is the opposite of what the issue asks for. The PR's tests only check the visible text, so they pass anyway.

own_checks.check: [[Getting Started|read the guide]] has the same href as [[Getting Started]] and shows the label
own_checks.command: python -c "import markdown; print(markdown.markdown('[[Getting Started|read the guide]]', extensions=['wikilinks']))"

own_checks.check: base_url, end_url and html_class apply to the target, not the label
own_checks.output_excerpt: c (expected the href to be /w/A_b.html)

findings.title: URL is built from the label instead of the target
findings.evidence: The PR sets `label = (m.group(2) or m.group(1)).strip()` and then calls `build_url(label, ...)`. The URL is therefore derived from the display text. With `[[Getting Started|read the guide]]` the output was `read the guide`. The issue requires the same URL as `[[Getting Started]]`, which is `/Getting_Started/`. A custom `build_url` also receives the label instead of the target.

findings.title: Tests only check the link text, not the href
findings.evidence: Both new tests use `assertIn('>read the guide', html)`. Neither checks the href, and neither covers `base_url`, `end_url`, a custom `build_url`, or a plain `[[Page]]`. They pass even though the URL is wrong.

notes: The label regex `[\w0-9_ -]+` rejects punctuation, so `[[A|b-c!]]` is left as literal text. Consider allowing wider label characters.
